models.name: dinov2_pet
models.source: tools/build/dinov2_pet_export.py — fp32 ONNX export of AvitoTech/DINO-v2-small-for-animal-identification (Hugging Face), CLS-token re-ID head
models.license: See the AvitoTech/DINO-v2-small-for-animal-identification model card; DINOv2 upstream is Apache-2.0
models.reason: Unlike the OpenCV Zoo YOLOX detector and the InsightFace buffalo_l pack, this ONNX has no upstream download URL — it is produced by a dev-only tool that needs torch + transformers. The `url` above is our own re-publication as a release asset on this repository, and it is what makes this weight behave like every other one: fetched once into the cache on first use, hash-verified against the `sha256` here. That release is permanent, since removing or retagging it would break both reproducible builds and first-run downloads for every version referencing this hash.

models.name: adaface
models.source: tools/build/adaface_export.py — fp32 ONNX export of marcelo-victor/adaface_ir101_webface12m (Hugging Face), AdaFace IR-101 trained on WebFace12M; exports both the 512-d L2-normalized embedding and the feature norm
models.license: AdaFace code is MIT — (c) 2022 Minchul Kim et al., https://github.com/mk-minchul/AdaFace — but these weights are trained on WebFace12M (a WebFace260M subset) and carry its non-commercial academic research terms. See packaging/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md.
models.reason: Same situation as dinov2_pet: no upstream ONNX exists, only a torch checkpoint, so this repository re-publishes the export as a release asset and the app fetches it once on first use. It is doubly load-bearing here because its second output — the feature norm — is the quality signal the FIQA gate (trove/faces/fiqa.py) tiers every face with; without it faces are all BORDERLINE and nothing can seed a cluster core.

models.name: ppocr_det
models.source: PaddleOCR PP-OCRv6 small text detection, as published by RapidAI at https://www.modelscope.cn/models/RapidAI/RapidOCR/resolve/v3.9.2/onnx/PP-OCRv6/det/PP-OCRv6_det_small.onnx — byte-identical to the copy inside the rapidocr 3.9.2 wheel
models.license: Apache-2.0. Engineering by RapidAI (https://github.com/RapidAI/RapidOCR); weights are Baidu's, released with PaddleOCR (https://github.com/PaddlePaddle/PaddleOCR). No non-commercial clause.
models.reason: Unlike dinov2_pet and adaface this weight *does* have an upstream URL, and it used to need neither URL nor manifest entry because it shipped inside the rapidocr wheel. That was 26.5 MB of compressed installer — the single largest item in the whole Python payload, larger than scipy or OpenCV — carried by every user for a feature most never enable. It is mirrored here rather than fetched from ModelScope directly for the same reason the two exports are: the manifest pins exact bytes forever, and the upstream `v3.9.2` path is RapidAI's to retag. Measured at ~1 MB/s from ModelScope on a European connection, which is the other half of the argument.

models.name: ppocr_rec
models.source: PaddleOCR PP-OCRv6 small text recognition, as published by RapidAI at https://www.modelscope.cn/models/RapidAI/RapidOCR/resolve/v3.9.2/onnx/PP-OCRv6/rec/PP-OCRv6_rec_small.onnx — byte-identical to the copy inside the rapidocr 3.9.2 wheel
models.license: Apache-2.0. Engineering by RapidAI (https://github.com/RapidAI/RapidOCR); weights are Baidu's, released with PaddleOCR (https://github.com/PaddlePaddle/PaddleOCR). No non-commercial clause.
models.reason: The largest of the three, and the one that carries the charset: 18,708 characters as ONNX metadata, including every Spanish accent, which is why Search by picture text needs no separate per-language weight (ADR 0019). Mirrored for the same reason as ppocr_det.

models.name: ppocr_cls
models.source: PaddleOCR PP-OCR mobile angle classifier, as published by RapidAI at https://www.modelscope.cn/models/RapidAI/RapidOCR/resolve/v3.9.2/onnx/PP-OCRv4/cls/ch_ppocr_mobile_v2.0_cls_mobile.onnx — byte-identical to the copy inside the rapidocr 3.9.2 wheel
models.license: Apache-2.0. Engineering by RapidAI (https://github.com/RapidAI/RapidOCR); weights are Baidu's, released with PaddleOCR (https://github.com/PaddlePaddle/PaddleOCR). No non-commercial clause.
models.reason: Half a megabyte, and the app never calls it: trove/text/ocr.py drives detection and recognition directly and never asks for orientation. It is here because `RapidOCR.__init__` builds all three sessions unconditionally, so a missing classifier is a constructor failure rather than a degraded reading. Cheaper to fetch than to fork the constructor.

models.name: bergamot_wasm
models.reason: The only one of these four that is a runtime rather than a weight, but it travels with them: without the WASM the three model files are unreadable, so splitting them across two tiers could only produce a half-installed translator. Served to the page by the /vendor route out of the cache (trove/web/routes/static.py), not imported by Python at all.

models.name: bergamot_es_en_model
models.source: Spanish-to-English Firefox Translations model, published by Mozilla — https://github.com/mozilla/translations
models.reason: Used only to translate a Spanish query before embedding it, which happens only on a description search — so this belongs to Search by description, a feature that already downloads 689 MB. It used to sit in trove/web/vendor/ inside the wheel, which meant every user carried 15.9 MB of compressed installer for a feature they might never enable, while the users who *did* enable it would not have noticed the same bytes arriving inside a 689 MB fetch. The page verifies these hashes again on its own side (trove/web/vendor/translation-es-en.json), so a corrupt copy is refused twice.

models.name: bergamot_es_en_lex
models.source: Shortlist for the Spanish-to-English Firefox Translations model, published by Mozilla — https://github.com/mozilla/translations
models.reason: Half of the same model as bergamot_es_en_model; see there.

models.name: bergamot_es_en_vocab
models.source: SentencePiece vocabulary for the Spanish-to-English Firefox Translations model, published by Mozilla — https://github.com/mozilla/translations
models.reason: Half of the same model as bergamot_es_en_model; see there.
